observedOn: an isolated v0.5.1.1 lab engine on a development host (its own volume and root key, reached through an ssh tunnel), in a throwaway account deleted afterwards (written here as `evimed`); it held only records written for this recording
fixtureEvidence: Every file beside this one is a verbatim exchange recorded by `packages/contracts/openviking/record.mjs` against that running server: `request` is what the script sent (the root key replaced by the placeholder `recorded-against-a-real-server`), `status` and `response` are what the server answered, re-indented and otherwise untouched. MCP answers are text/event-stream bodies and are kept as the raw text. `_index.json` lists every file with its route and status. Nothing was authored: a file whose status is an error is the error the server gave. Two files could not be recorded again and are the v0.5.0 recordings, `recordedFrom` saying so: `task-failed.json` and `archive-failed-marker-read.json` (a commit whose extraction fails because the model endpoint answers 402 needs a gateway that does).
shape: Unlike the three files the repository holds today (bare response bodies), each fixture here is `{ note, recordedFrom, request: { method, path, headers, body }, status, contentType, response }`. The five exchanges the product already depends on are re-recorded at v0.5.1.1 as health.json, find.json, find-unauthenticated.json, fs-ls.json, content-write-create.json / content-write-replace.json and fs-delete.json; their `response` is the bare body the existing contract test reads.

configuration.vlm: provider openai, model deepseek-flash, thinking disabled through extra_request_body, max_tokens 16384, reached through the deployment's model gateway shape (a service bearer; the provider key is not in the engine)
configuration.memory: extraction_enabled true, extraction_output_format python, custom_templates_dir = the directory of deploy/web/openviking/memory-templates, prefetch_search_topn 10, session_auto_commit enabled (check 300 s, 50 files/s)
configuration.server.user_config_defaults: memory_policy.memory_types = profile, preferences, entities, corrections, project_context, decisions, follow_ups, project_facts; auto_commit_policy = idle 900 s, 150000 tokens, 100 messages
configuration.container: the lab's own container (not hardened as production is), the built-in bot on, no identity shim

observations: Trusted mode with a root key still requires X-API-Key on every request (find-unauthenticated.json), as at v0.4.19, v0.4.23 and v0.5.0; the refusal's message reads 'Missing API Key in trusted mode. Send X-API-Key with the value of server.root_api_key…' on v0.5.1.1.

A session id chosen by the client is accepted (session-create.json uses the DSH plugin's `dsh-<kernel session id>` form); creating it again answers 409 ALREADY_EXISTS, which the plugin treats as success. Session metadata (session-read.json) carries `last_idle_commit_accepted_at` since v0.5.1.

A commit answers at once with a task id; the task's token_usage and memories_extracted are cumulative over the session, not per commit (compare task-completed.json with task-completed-no-operations.json).

memory_diff.json is written for a commit that changes nothing (memory-diff-read-no-operations.json) and is read through content/read as JSON text; a failed commit leaves .failed.json instead (archive-failed-marker-read.json) and is never retried by the server.
fs/ls?recursive=true stops three levels down; fs/tree takes level_limit and returns tags when include_tags=true (fs-tree.json).

search/search in context mode with purpose=coding retrieves by bucket (events, entities, preferences, experiences, resources, skills): a custom memory type is not returned (search-context-as-plugin.json). Without purpose and quotas it retrieves flat and reports custom types under category `memories` (search-context-flat.json).
stats/memories answers account-wide totals to any user (stats-memories.json).

The admin routes do not know a trusted user until it is registered: settings and deletion answer 404 `User not found` for a user who already has files (admin-user-settings-get-unregistered.json, admin-user-delete-unregistered.json). POST /admin/accounts/{account}/users registers it; a second registration answers 409.
An admin route that names a user in its URL refuses a different X-OpenViking-User (400); with the account header and no user header it is accepted (admin-user-delete-no-user-header.json).

A settings PATCH that carries no memory_types leaves the user with every registered type, the deployment default no longer applying (admin-user-settings-pause.json); admin-user-settings-patch-with-types.json is the form that keeps the allowlist.

While a user is being deleted a request as that user answered 412 FAILED_PRECONDITION on v0.5.0 (no recording of it is kept). On v0.5.1.1 the same request, made at once after the 202 for a user with one file, answered 404: the deletion had already finished, so the 412 window is not guaranteed and the client waits for either (request-during-user-deletion.json, request-after-user-deletion.json).
The MCP endpoint answers text/event-stream with one `message` event and sets no Mcp-Session-Id; tools/list offers 20 tools to a USER, list_users among them (mcp-tools-list.json).
The MCP `remember` tool creates a session named mcp-store-<id>, commits it and names the task id in its text answer; the session stays until it is deleted (session-delete-remember-store.json).

`content/write` with `mode: create` on a file that exists is a 200 that overwrites it from v0.5.1 (content-write-create-conflict.json; it was a 409 ALREADY_EXISTS on v0.5.0): `create` is an alias of `replace`. `replace` on a file that is not there creates it, parents included. Both under `memories/` as well as under `resources/`.
`fs` delete answers carry a `task_id` since v0.5.1 (the cleanup of the parent directory's summary); the client reads `estimated_deleted_count` only.

A commit's task result and its memory_diff.json keep the v0.5.0 shapes: the key paths of task-completed.json, task-completed-no-operations.json, memory-diff-read.json and memory-diff-read-no-operations.json are the same as in the v0.5.0 recordings.
notRecorded: task-failed.json and archive-failed-marker-read.json: an extraction whose model call is refused (402) needs a model gateway that refuses it; the lab's gateway is not this repository's to switch. They stay as recorded on v0.5.0.
